rv.q: Cole Escola’s wildly absurd, historically inaccurate farce has made its way from Broadway to the national tour, and the transition works beautifully.

rv.cn: Drew Sitton • Times of San Diego
rv.q: It is offensive and raunchy in the best way possible.
As feisty and foul-mouthed and queer and outrageous as “Oh, Mary!” ecstatically is, small theaters will be clamoring to do this show for decades.
I've never heard an audience at the Civic Theatre roar with more surprised laughter than I did on Wednesday, the official opening night of the Broadway play's national tour.
She takes Mary to a level of crazy that few performers would dare attempt, but it suits Escola's script perfectly.
Oh, Mary! is a farcical delight that revels in the incredible comic timing of underrated drag queen Alaska Thunderfuck.

cn.t: Critics hail this farcical delight as a laugh-out-loud smash, with Alaska Thunderfuck's comic timing and Cole Escola's sharp writing earning raves. The 80-minute romp delivers consistent hilarity that lives up to its Broadway hype.
